findings.description: The shared statistics dict of the wrapper is cleared and reused on every call, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function share and overwrite one stats dict.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function runs concurrently (threads) or recursively. The old code created a fresh per-call copy's statistics. Now stats.clear() wipes the in-progress stats of another call, and both calls write into one dict. Impact: corrupted attempt_number and delay_since_first_attempt, which are also read by the retrying logic, and the per-call isolation the comment above promises is broken.

findings.description: Async wrapper clears and reuses a single shared statistics dict for all concurrent invocations.
findings.rationale: Trigger: asyncio.gather of several calls to the same decorated coroutine function. Each call does stats.clear() and writes into the same dict, so stats from in-flight calls are reset and mixed. Impact: wrong attempt_number and start times, which affects wait and stop decisions that read statistics.
